title: Open mapping, closed graph and Zorn's lemma
summary: The open mapping theorem and its corollary, the bounded inverse theorem; products of Banach spaces; the closed graph theorem; partial orders, chains, Zorn's lemma and Hamel bases, preparing for Hahn–Banach.

objectives.description: State the open mapping theorem and the bounded inverse theorem with hypotheses, and use them to compare two complete norms.
State the closed graph theorem and use it to prove boundedness of an operator defined on a Banach space.
Explain why the unbounded inverse of the Volterra operator does not contradict the bounded inverse theorem.
State Zorn's lemma precisely and use it to show every vector space has a Hamel basis.

preparation.description: Read lecture 4 notes pages 1–2: the Open Mapping Theorem (Theorem 37) with its proof, Corollary 38 and Proposition 39.
Read Theorem 40 (Closed Graph Theorem) and Remark 41 (page 3).
Read Definitions 42–46 on partial orders, chains, Zorn's lemma and Hamel bases (page 4).

activities.title: Lecture 4: open mapping, closed graph, Zorn
activities.instructions: Read the lesson with lecture 4 of the notes. The proof of the open mapping theorem has two halves; identify which half uses Baire and which uses completeness of the domain directly.

activities.title: Tutorial: consequences of the open mapping theorem
activities.instructions: Attempt exercises 1 and 2. In each, write the hypothesis of the theorem you invoke in full before invoking it.

activities.title: Explain: Zorn's lemma and Hamel bases

exitCheck.description: Exercise 1 accepted: the bounded inverse theorem applied to the identity map to show two complete comparable norms are equivalent, with both completeness hypotheses stated.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A bijective bounded operator always has a bounded inverse.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Only between Banach spaces. The Volterra operator onto its range (with the sup norm) is bijective and bounded, but the range is not complete and the inverse (differentiation) is unbounded.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The closed graph theorem says a continuous operator has a closed graph.
commonMisconceptions.correction: That direction is elementary. The content of the theorem is the converse: between Banach spaces, a linear operator with closed graph is bounded.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Zorn's lemma can be proved from the other axioms.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It is equivalent to the axiom of choice; the notes take it as an axiom. Its use here (Hamel bases, Hahn–Banach) is legitimate but non-constructive.
